# 1 Enoch Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** I saw where all the winds are stored. I saw how God had used them to build the whole creation and to anchor the foundations of the earth.

**2** I saw the cornerstone of the earth. I saw the four winds that hold up the earth and the dome of the sky.

**3** I saw how the winds stretch the sky's vault tight and keep their position in the space between heaven and earth — they are the pillars that hold the sky up.

**4** I saw the winds of heaven that turn the sun and all the stars in their circles and bring them to their setting-place.

**5** I saw the wind on the earth pushing the clouds. I saw the pathways of the angels. I saw, at the very edge of the earth, the vault of heaven overhead.

**6** I moved on and came to a place that burns around the clock — day and night, without pause. There were seven mountains there, made of glittering precious stones — three mountains facing east and three facing south.

**7** The eastern mountains: one was made of multicolored stone, one of pearl, and one of jacinth. The southern mountains were made of red stone.

**8** But the central mountain rose all the way to heaven — it looked like the throne of God itself. It was made of alabaster, and the top of that throne was capped with sapphire.

**9** I saw a blazing fire there. Beyond these mountains lies the edge of the great earth — the place where the sky meets its end.

**10** I saw a vast and deep abyss. In it were columns of fire from heaven, and I watched shafts of fire plunging down through the abyss — immeasurable in height and depth.

**11** Beyond the abyss I came to a place where there was no sky overhead and no solid ground below. No water, no birds — nothing. It was a desolate and terrifying wasteland.

**12** I saw seven stars in that place, blazing like huge mountains of fire. When I asked about them,

**13** the angel told me: "This place is the far end of heaven and earth. It has been turned into a prison for the stars and for the armies of heaven.

**14** The stars you see rolling in the fire are those who disobeyed the Lord's command at the very beginning — they failed to appear when they were supposed to, at their appointed times.

**15** God was furious with them. He has bound them here until the time when their sentence is complete — ten thousand years."

**16** Then Uriel said to me: "This is also where the angels who had sex with women will be imprisoned. Their spirits are out there now, taking many different forms, corrupting humanity and leading people astray into offering sacrifices to demons as though they were gods. But they will end up here — standing in this place until the great Day of Judgment, when they will be judged and destroyed."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 18 is the most cosmologically rich chapter in the first journey. The first half (vv. 1–9) describes the infrastructure of creation — winds as structural elements, the world-mountain as throne. The second half (vv. 10–16) reveals the prison at the end of the world — the abyss where disobedient stars are already imprisoned and the Watchers will join them. The chapter brings the Book of Watchers' judgment narrative full circle: the Watchers who fell will be imprisoned in the same abyss as the disobedient stars.*
